evidence.excerpt:
Definition 3.5 Pairwise calibration

    The pairwise calibration between two models is the Kendall’s 𝜏-b (Kendall, 1945) between their
    confidence-difference and performance-difference vectors across items, using the tie-corrected
    𝜏-b variant so that pairs the models agree on do not attenuate the correlation.

    This is pairwise calibration in the discriminatory sense (Def. 3.1). For each model pair and
each item, we ask whether model A actually outperforms model B when A says “I can solve this”
and B says “I cannot” and vice versa. A concordant pair is one where the more-confident model
performs better; a discordant pair is the reverse. Positive 𝜏 therefore means a model’s confidence
carries information about its own capability relative to the other model. Aggregating 𝜏 across

mean sitting significantly below this null mean (green distribution in Fig. 5, with the exception of
MathBench) is the central paper result: almost all observed pairwise calibration is shared rather

facts.description: MMLU-Pro12032题14学科随机取1000，使用LLM按gold语义等价评分。

evidence.excerpt:
D.2 MMLU-Pro
We use the MMLU-Pro test split (Wang et al., 2024), which contains 12,032 items across 14 subject
categories, randomly sampled to 1,000. The question stem is the question specification, and the ten
answer options (A–J) are the optional context. We use an LLM judge to grade semantic equivalence
to the ground truth answer.
